directive.name: coding
directive.description: Code quality standards: architecture, type safety, error handling, declarative style, and documentation

context.principle: Policy belongs in orchestrators, mechanism in capabilities
Dependencies must form a DAG. Flow: Computer <- Capability <- Orchestrator
Every module must be categorized with suffix: .computer.ts, .capability.ts, .orchestrator.ts

Actively decompose orchestrators. At ~500 lines or when 2+ unrelated concerns share a file, split into domain orchestrators immediately. Don't let orchestrators grow — when you notice complexity accumulating, that's the signal to split now, not later.
Entry points should be thin composition roots that wire domain orchestrators together

Explicit dependency injection via factory function parameters. Never import and construct a dependency internally — receive it from the caller. The composition root is the only place that wires concrete implementations together.
Side effects (I/O, network, file system, randomness, time) live exclusively in capabilities. Computers are pure. Orchestrators coordinate but delegate all side effects to capabilities.
One public factory per module. Each .computer.ts, .capability.ts, .orchestrator.ts file exports a single create* function and its associated types. Keeps modules focused and the DAG easy to trace.
Never use any — use unknown and narrow with type guard functions (isX returning value is Type).
All exported functions must have explicit return types
Use branded types for domain identifiers (TaskId, ProjectId, etc.)

Make illegal states unrepresentable. Design types so invalid combinations cannot be constructed — not validated at runtime. Use discriminated unions for states, not boolean flags. If a completedAt date only makes sense when status is 'done', the type must enforce that structurally.

Parse, don't validate. At system boundaries (user input, file reads, API responses), transform untyped data into typed domain objects once using Result<T, E>, then trust the types everywhere downstream. Capabilities own parsing and return Result for expected failures. Only throw for bugs. Never re-check what the type system already guarantees.

Total functions — every function handles every possible input and always returns a value. No functions that silently return undefined for unexpected input. Switch on discriminated unions must be exhaustive using default with never. Combined with Result types, this eliminates partial functions entirely.
No enums. Use string literal unions or const objects with as const. Enums generate runtime code, don't compose, and fight against declarative style.

Prefer declarative over imperative. Express WHAT not HOW. Use map/filter/reduce over mutation loops, ternaries over if/else assignments, data pipelines over step-by-step procedures. Use early returns and guard clauses to keep code flat — never nest more than 2 levels deep.

Compose small functions, don't configure large ones. Build complex behavior by piping simple transformations — not by adding parameters, flags, and options to one function. Under 20 lines ideal, over 40 is a smell. If a section needs a comment, extract it.
Readonly by default. All arrays, tuples, and interface properties should be readonly. Never mutate function arguments. Mutability is the exception that must be justified. Computers must be pure.
No floating promises. Use Promise.all for independent concurrent work.

Use Record/object lookups instead of if/else chains or switch for value mapping. When mapping one set of values to another, a const Record is declarative, exhaustive (with satisfies), and eliminates branching logic entirely.

Data and behavior are separate. Data is plain readonly objects and types. Behavior is functions that accept and return data. No classes — classes bundle state and behavior, hide mutation behind this, and resist composition. Use factory functions that return plain objects with explicit interfaces.
Naming: create* for factories, is*/has*/should* for booleans, handle*/on* for event handlers.
All exported symbols must have multi-line TSDoc. @param tags use hyphen: @param name - description

When renaming or refactoring: delete the old thing, update every caller, done. No re-exports under old names, no wrapper functions that translate old args to new, no "keep both" transition periods, no deprecated markers. If something changes, it changes everywhere in the same commit. Callers that break get fixed immediately — not "later."
All code changes must pass build verification before completion
This project builds festinalente. .claude/ and .opencode/ contain built output — edit source in apps/festinalente/src/content/.

process.rule: Identify architectural layers of affected files and verify DAG
Plan orchestrator structure — identify domains, decide single vs multiple orchestrators
Identify side effects and confine them to capabilities. Computers and orchestrators must remain free of I/O.
Categorize every new module with correct suffix, wrap pure functions in computer factories
Inject all dependencies via factory parameters. Never import and construct internally.

Design types that make illegal states unrepresentable: branded IDs, discriminated unions where data only exists in valid states, options objects for >2 params. If a combination shouldn't exist, the type must prevent it structurally.
Design error handling: identify which operations can fail, use Result types with specific error variants
Design data transformations as declarative pipelines. Plan function decomposition: small, single-purpose functions.
For renames, moves, and signature changes: delete the old thing, update every caller, in the same step. No re-exports, no overloads, no transition periods.
Verify each task step with appropriate build command
Run all relevant build commands for modified packages
Scan for forbidden patterns before review

Verify orchestrator sizes. Any orchestrator approaching ~500 lines or mixing unrelated concerns must be decomposed into domain orchestrators before the task is complete. This is not optional — do not defer decomposition to a future task.

check.expect: Festina Lente package builds successfully (exit code 0)

check.reason: No enums — use string literal unions or const objects with as const
No classes — use factory functions with closures
Computers must be pure — no I/O, no randomness, no time
Orchestrators delegate I/O to capabilities — don't do it directly
Use map/filter/reduce/for...of instead of index loops
Computers are pure — return Result instead
Single-line TSDoc on exports — use multi-line format
No re-export aliases — rename at source, update all callers
Comments about old code signal a compat shim — delete the old thing entirely
If it needs removing, remove it now — not "later"
